comments.body:
## RCA (Phase 1 complete — root cause proven)

**Proven root cause.** `tests/conftest.py`'s `_no_repo_root_leaks` autouse fixture diffs REPO_ROOT's top-level entries around each test and `pytest.fail`s on any new entry, filtered only by `_is_coverage_artifact(name)` (conftest.py:337/363). `.pytest_cache` is NOT in that exemption, so when pytest materializes a `.pytest_cache/` dir under REPO_ROOT during a test's wall-clock window (floor-leg pytest writes it despite `-p no:cacheprovider`), the after−before diff contains `.pytest_cache` → the guard fails at teardown: `New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test: ['.pytest_cache']` (conftest.py:379). `.pytest_cache/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:7`) and produced by the pytest framework, not by any test body — the identical class the guard already exempts for coverage.py's data files (`.coverage`/`.coverage.*`/`coverage.xml`).

**Proof (discriminating experiment).** Drove the REAL `_no_repo_root_leaks` teardown against a scratch root with `_REPO_ROOT` patched (existing `_drive_leak_guard` harness): with only `.pytest_cache/` appearing, the guard FAILS (returns the leak message) — confirming the mechanism is the missing exemption, not pytest writing the dir per se. Rules out the "genuine pollution" alternative: a mixed case (`.pytest_cache` + a real `stray_report.json`) also failed and named BOTH, showing the guard cannot currently distinguish the framework artifact from real pollution. RED captured in `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py::test_leak_guard_exempts_pytest_cache` (+ `_still_fails_on_real_pollution_beside_pytest_cache`).

**Defect legitimacy = `defect` (omission).** The guard's own contract (its `_is_coverage_artifact` docstring + this ticket's ACs) is authoritative: framework-produced, gitignored artifacts are not test leaks. `.pytest_cache` is that class and was never exempted — an omission, not a regression.

**Defect origin / attribution.** Scope-of-work (omission) attribution. The "framework/gitignored artifact is not a leak" carve-out was introduced by task **8d36** (`8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd`, commit `f943c7ef5884`, curricular-brickred-ratfish), which established exactly this exemption and its rationale ("plugin-produced + gitignored, not test leaks") but enumerated only coverage.py's files — the `.pytest_cache` case falls under that same acceptance and was omitted. The guard itself predates any exemption (origin `4c79-3873`). Change **2420** (`47713c44`) did not introduce the defect — it merely EXPOSED this latent omission by removing the floor leg's build `TypeError`, letting the floor `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` unit tier actually run. Close-class therefore `preexisting`; `--caused-by=8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd`.

**Fix direction (portable, per AC #2).** Exempt the framework/tooling cache-artifact class (`.pytest_cache` + sibling gitignored tool caches: `.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.mutmut-cache`, `__pycache__`) alongside coverage artifacts — an allowlist that still fails on any genuine new entry. No dependence on a specific pytest version or CI provider.

## Problem

Surfaced while fixing `anatomical-arbored-oyster` (e3e0-2e7c-b280-4b4a). With the floor leg's build `TypeError` removed, `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` runs the unit tier and emits teardown ERRORs:

```
ERROR at teardown of test_link_success_noop_and_unlink_lines
Failed: New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test: ['.pytest_cache']
tests/conftest.py:379: Failed
```

## Root cause (to confirm)

`tests/conftest.py`'s REPO_ROOT-pollution guard (~line 379) asserts no new entries appear under the repo root during a test. On the floor leg a `.pytest_cache` directory materializes under REPO_ROOT despite `-p no:cacheprovider`, tripping the guard at teardown for several tests. Likely a floor-version pytest / plugin writing a cache dir the guard does not exempt, or a test invoking a subprocess pytest. Needs confirmation of which layer creates `.pytest_cache` and whether the guard should exempt it.

## Fix direction

Either exempt `.pytest_cache` from the REPO_ROOT-pollution guard (if benign) or stop the floor-leg pytest from writing it under REPO_ROOT. Test-hygiene; likely mechanical once the writer is identified.

## Evidence
- Mirror run 33299427686: `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` job 99224621821 — multiple `ERROR at teardown ... New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test: ['.pytest_cache']`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The floor `sweep (declared lower-bound resolution)` leg has no `.pytest_cache` REPO_ROOT-pollution teardown errors.
- [ ] The pollution guard's treatment of `.pytest_cache` is portable (no dependence on a specific pytest version or CI provider).

file_impact.reason: Exempt the gitignored tool-cache class (.pytest_cache + siblings) from the _no_repo_root_leaks REPO_ROOT-pollution guard via a new _is_framework_artifact predicate, so framework artifacts no longer trip the floor-leg teardown.
Regression tests driving the REAL guard: .pytest_cache is exempted (guard passes) while genuine pollution beside it still fails and is named.
